_why: A/B of the burn's annotate model (tools/puzzle_worker.sh via ANNOTATE_MODEL/ANNOTATE_EFFORT): the next 20 keyed puzzles in burn queue order, each run three ways through the burn's Annotate path (worker_annotate + worker_finish, commit stubbed) in scratch clones. eq_tokens weights in 1, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, out 5 (the burn token analysis's quota weights, same for both models); usd uses list prices Opus $5/$25, Sonnet $3/$15 per M. A check passes first time when its summary has no ERROR; spotless = no warnings either. Blind judge: 10 clues, labels shuffled, judged against cryptic-hint-rungs-no-giveaways + cryptic-surface-is-a-joke; rank points 2/1/0 per clue.

judge.notes: All parse the cryptic definition correctly; A's definitionFit names Father Christmas outright, while B and C say 'gift-bringer'. C pins the setter's reading on the single word 'sacked', which is the sharpest teaching.

judge2.notes: A's definitionFit names Father Christmas outright; B and C describe the gift-bringer without naming him. C isolates 'sacked' as the misdirected word in its own block, which is the cleanest teaching.

judge.notes: All take the alternate letters of 'this does' correctly. B alone points out the semi-&lit (the whole clue also describes the tide). A's definitionFit opens 'The tide is...', which gives the answer away.

judge2.notes: B alone sees the semi-&lit self-reference ('this' = the clue's own words) and its definitionFit avoids the answer; A explains the 'regularly' misdirection but its definitionFit opens 'The tide is'. C has no walkthrough.

judge.notes: C's ELECT+RON charade and B's double definition both teach the split. A calls it a cryptic definition 'sound of' and puts 'elect Ron' in its surface field. All three definitionFits name 'electron', and B's walkthrough also spells ELECT RON.

judge2.notes: B's double definition (with 'in' as the link) is the right reading. C's charade has 'campaign slogan' giving ELECT, which is forced. A's surface field ('elect Ron') and walkthrough hand over the answer, and it wrongly calls the split a sound. All three definitionFits name 'electron'.

judge.notes: C is the only one with a block for 'a' and a cleaner definition ('Mediterranean one', with a note that one = island). A and B put an A in the assembly that no block accounts for and lean on double duty. A explains 'one' better than B, whose surface is flat. All definitionFits name Sardinia.

judge2.notes: C is the cleanest parse: SARDIN+I+A, with 'a' as its own block and 'Mediterranean one' as the definition. Its walkthrough also explains the island/I misdirection, though its block note 'sardine without its last letter' names the fish. A and B make 'a' do double duty with no block for it. A at least explains 'one' pointing back to island; B's surface is flat. All three definitionFits name Sardinia.

judge.notes: The PINS reversal is identical in all three. A and C explain the phrasal-verb misdirection of 'Fixes up' well, and A's 'stitching up a wound' surface is the best. B's surface and its claim that the trick is 'Fixes is a verb not a noun' miss the misdirection. All definitionFits start 'A snip is'.

judge2.notes: All three parse it identically. A best explains how the phrasal verb 'fixes up' splits, with a vivid surface (stitching a wound). C says the same more briefly. B's surface is muddled and its walkthrough's verb/noun remark is confused. All three definitionFits say 'A snip is'.

judge.notes: The parses are identical; A's longer definition, which takes in 'this is', is acceptable. A's definitionFit describes Scott's novel without naming it, whereas B and C begin 'Rob Roy is'. C explains the dismissal misdirection more clearly than B.

judge2.notes: A's definitionFit describes Scott's 1817 novel without naming it, while B and C write 'Rob Roy is...'. A folds 'this is' into the definition, which is acceptable. B's walkthrough also says the answer is a Scott novel.

judge.notes: A gives RU to 'sport' and RL to 'two codes', which is wrong: both come from 'sport, two codes'. B and C have the right shared blocks. C's definitionFit does not name 'rural', while A's and B's do.

judge2.notes: A gives RU to 'sport' alone and RL to 'two codes', which misallocates the clue words. B and C correctly use 'sport - two codes' for both. C's indicator note wrongly says 'the codes' wrap round the A. B's surface reading (a rustic game under two sets of rules) is best.

judge.notes: The parses are identical and teaching is thin across the board. C's definitionFit ties 'exploitation' to the market gap best. B's walkthrough only repeats the RA note and its surface is a paraphrase. All definitionFits name arbitrage.

judge2.notes: The parses are identical and none explains the misdirection. C's surface paraphrase is the most natural, and its definitionFit ties back to 'exploitation'. B's surface just restates the clue and its walkthrough is trivial.

judge.notes: A correctly finds REVERE hidden across 'foR EVER (and) EVEr', with 'and' skipped, 'receives' as the indicator and 'praise' as the definition. B treats the skipped 'and' as a link word and has an odd 'A normal clue' line. C wrongly takes 'receives praise' as the definition and has no indicator. All definitionFits name revere.

judge2.notes: A and B read it as a hidden run R+EVER+E skipping 'and', with ND inserted per the preamble. A's walkthrough states this most clearly. C has no indicator and takes 'receives praise' as the definition of REVERE. All three definitionFits say 'To revere', which spells out the pre-insertion answer. I'm unsure of the true parse.

judge.notes: A and C correctly have E inside an anagram of MASS (ASS-E-M), then B and LED. C adds a walkthrough on the 'special mass' misdirection, which A lacks. B anagrams MASSE, leaving 'with' and 'in' unaccounted for. All definitionFits use 'assembled'.

judge2.notes: The right parse is E inside an anagram of MASS, then B+LED. A and C have it, with 'in' as the container indicator. B anagrams MASSE and leaves 'in'/'with' unaccounted for. C adds a walkthrough on how 'special mass' misleads. All three definitionFits name 'assembled'.

blind_note: Two independent Opus judges, same pack of 10 clues newly annotated in all three arms (one per puzzle). Both judges flagged definitionFit naming the answer in most versions of every arm, so the giveaway counts do not separate the arms. Blog checks compared 481 clue facts per arm with 0 disagreements: annotate_check already enforces blog agreement, so it cannot discriminate. All 20 puzzles were keyed (no cold solve fits the time box), so answer accuracy is 0 changed answers in every arm by construction.
